directAnswer: St. Siricius was pope from 384 to 399 and the author of the earliest papal decretal that survives complete, a letter to Bishop Himerius of Tarragona in Spain. In that and later letters he gave binding rulings on baptism, penance, ordination, and the continence of clergy. He also condemned the monk Jovinian and dedicated the rebuilt Basilica of St. Paul Outside the Walls.

sections.h2: The Letter to Himerius of Tarragona
paras: Siricius, a Roman who had served as a deacon under Liberius and Damasus, was elected in December 384. Soon after, a letter from Himerius, bishop of Tarragona, arrived asking about disciplinary questions in the Spanish churches. Siricius answered in a letter usually dated to early 385.

This reply is the oldest surviving papal decretal, an authoritative ruling meant to be observed as law. It addressed whether converts baptized by Arians needed rebaptism (they did not, but were received by the laying on of hands), set Easter and Pentecost as the normal seasons for baptism, regulated public penance, and laid down requirements for those seeking ordination.

The decretal is best known for insisting that bishops, priests, and deacons live in perpetual continence. Many clergy at that time were married, and Siricius did not dissolve those marriages, but he required that married clergy abstain from relations with their wives after ordination.

He presented this not as a novelty but as an obligation flowing from the service of the altar. Historians regard the letter as the first papal decree on the subject, and it shaped Western discipline on clerical celibacy for centuries. A Roman synod in 386 repeated similar rules and communicated them to the bishops of Africa.

Around 390, a monk named Jovinian taught that virginity was no holier than marriage and that fasting brought no special merit. Siricius condemned him at a Roman synod, and St. Ambrose and the bishops of Milan concurred. At the same time, Siricius defended the dignity of marriage against extreme ascetic views.

His relationship with Jerome was cool. Jerome left Rome in 385, not long after Siricius's election, and later wrote of him without warmth. With Ambrose, the dominant bishop of northern Italy, Siricius maintained cooperative ties.
The emperors had begun building a much larger basilica over the tomb of St. Paul on the road to Ostia. In 390 Siricius dedicated it, and an inscription naming him is still preserved in the basilica.
Siricius died on November 26, 399, and was buried in the Catacomb of Priscilla on the Via Salaria. His feast is kept on that day.

keyFacts: Wrote the oldest surviving papal decretal, to Himerius of Tarragona (c. 385)
First papal decree requiring continence of bishops, priests, and deacons
Condemned Jovinian at a Roman synod around 390
Dedicated the rebuilt St. Paul Outside the Walls in 390; feast day November 26

faqs.question: What is a papal decretal, and why is Siricius important for it?
faqs.answer: A decretal is a papal letter giving an authoritative ruling on a point of church discipline. Siricius's letter to Himerius of Tarragona is the oldest one that survives complete.

faqs.question: Did Pope Siricius require priests to be celibate?
faqs.answer: He required bishops, priests, and deacons to live in continence. Married clergy kept their marriages but were to abstain from marital relations after ordination. It was the first papal decree on the matter.

faqs.question: Who was Jovinian, whom Siricius condemned?
faqs.answer: Jovinian was a Roman monk who argued that virginity and fasting had no greater merit than marriage and ordinary living. Siricius condemned his teaching at a Roman synod around 390.
